name: s11-decorator
title: What @decorator really does
spec: Top: code chip @deco above def f(): ... with an equals sign to f = deco(f). Below: a box deco(f) returns wrapper. A call flow f() -> wrapper -> does extra work -> calls the original f -> returns its result. Green note: functools.wraps keeps the name and docstring.
alt: How a decorator rebinds a function
cap: A decorator is a function that takes a function and returns a replacement, usually a wrapper.

name: s11-lookup
title: Attribute lookup order with descriptors
spec: A top-to-bottom list of four ordered steps for obj.attr: 1 data descriptor on the class (has __set__), 2 the instance __dict__, 3 non-data descriptor or plain class attribute, 4 __getattr__ as the last resort. Number circles. Orange highlight on step 1: it beats the instance dictionary.
cap: Lookup order: a data descriptor wins over the instance dictionary, which wins over non-data descriptors.

name: s11-classcreate
title: What the class statement does
spec: A left-to-right flow: class body runs in a fresh namespace ; Python collects name, bases and namespace ; calls type(name, bases, namespace) (or the metaclass) ; a class object is created and bound to the name. Orange note: __init_subclass__ and class decorators hook in here.
cap: The class statement runs the body, then calls type (or a metaclass) to build the class object.

name: s11-twotrees
title: The two inheritance trees
spec: Left tree (header is an instance of, dashed arrows): obj is an instance of Class, Class is an instance of type, type is an instance of type. Right tree (header inherits from, solid arrows): Class inherits from Base, Base inherits from object. A note: a metaclass is a subclass of type, and it changes how classes are built.
anchor: ### Metaclasses and the two-tree inheritance model
cap: Two trees: instances link to their classes, and classes link to their metaclass, while subclasses inherit from bases.
